clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10303 with a subject line describing an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army. The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer); this is not an until-date, so no inclusive or exclusive reading arises. The thirty-day report deadline is not an end; the board's report is dated January 25, 1952 (held report title page), after which the order was functionally spent but remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10303 at 16 FR 11321, in the Federal Register of November 8, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10303, is signed November 6, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Nov. 7, 1951. Text: the order recites a dispute between the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad Company, the Chicago & North Western Railway Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and all other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, carriers under Federal management, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, and recites that by Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950 the President, through the Secretary of the Army, assumed possession, control and operation of those carriers' transportation systems. Invoking the Constitution and laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, and subject to that section, it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute. Its operative text then has three more sentences: a sentence that nothing in the order shall be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155; "The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order."; and a sentence requiring the Board, in performing its functions, to comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. Inventory: the dossier split the order into two clauses at the number 10155, which ends the sentence on the Secretary of the Army's authority. The order has no numbered paragraphs, so the inventory is corrected to one whole-order clause from the heading through the Defense Production Act sentence. Ending: Executive Order 12553, headed "Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986" and printed at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986 (held govinfo text layer), orders that "the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked"; its No. Subject table lists 10303 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between employees and transportation systems operated by the Secretary of the Army". The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is dated on signing, 1986-02-25; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of March 3, 1986 is not used. The enacting sentence has no exception or saving clause. Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (held text jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10303_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10303_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_502ff45635.txt) is titled as the report of the emergency board created November 6, 1951 by Executive Order 10303, and its title page is dated at Washington, D. C., January 25, 1952. The same report states that the parties obtained an extension of the time for the report after the hearings began late. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report date and the end of any statutory period are spent facts: the order was functionally spent once the board had reported, but it remained on the books until its express revocation. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records the Executive Order 12553 revocation and a cross-reference between this order and Executive Order 10155. The held-text number search found this number only in the Federal Register text file of the order's own printing and the front matter of the board's report.
